text:
maria: deploy-bot flagged a ~12% drop in embedding similarity on canary (slice=5%). deploy-bot suggests automated rollback to model:v2.4.1 unless suppressed. EU dedicated pools are still routing ~18% of embed traffic to canary. do we allow auto-rollback or do a staged/manual unwind? need thoughts and comms plan.

deploy-bot: Alert: metric 'embed_quality.delta' = 12.1% > threshold. Recommended action: auto-rollback to model:v2.4.1 in 60s. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-embeddings|rollback runbook> :warning:

arpit: don't auto-rollback. we have dedicated customers — that will cause a surprise model change for them. prefer staged: rollback hosted first, keep dedicated pinned while we notify and decide.

kevin: agree with staged approach. we can route hosted back to v2.4.1 and leave dedicated on v2.5.0 for committed pools. requires pin on the dedicated pools and a routing update. ops-oncall, can you take the pin if we decide to proceed?

ops-oncall: oncall here — i need explicit confirmation in this channel to suppress automated rollback and to act. which dedicated pool exactly? is it 'dedicated-eu-west1-prod'? also need product approval before changing dedicated customers' model.

sam: i'll ping the account execs for the 3 dedicated customers in EU now. if we don't hear back in 30m we should proceed with hosted-only rollback and publish a customer note + opt-in scheduled window for dedicated. i'll draft a short template and link it here. :phone:

lisa: proposed steps — short and actionable: 1) suppress deploy-bot auto-rollback (so we don't bounce) 2) rollback hosted slice to v2.4.1 3) post customer note + update release notes 4) monitor embed_quality and latency for 20m 5) decide on pinning dedicated pools. anyone disagree?

arpit: command to run for the hosted rollback (tested in staging):
```
redwoodctl rollout set-route --service embeddings --from model:v2.5.0 --to model:v2.4.1 --slice hosted --reason "canary embed quality regression"
```
This will not touch dedicated pools.

ops-oncall: suppressing auto-rollback now -> `deployctl suppress-rollback 1778801234 --reason "staged-hosted-rollback"` — done. :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: running hosted rollback command now. updating routing table for hosted slice -> v2.4.1. results: rollout started, 100 hosts updated in ~45s. monitoring ingress and p95.

deploy-bot: Action: automated rollback suppressed by ops-oncall. Hosted slice rollback initiated to model:v2.4.1. Telemetry: <https://telemetry.redwood/rollouts/1778801234|rollout link>.

sam: customer note template (short): "We observed a canary regression in embedding quality and rolled hosted traffic back to the previous model to maintain quality. Your dedicated pool has not been changed; if you'd like us to schedule a maintenance window to align models, reply here or contact your AE." Posted to #customer-comm-drafts: <https://docs.internal/comm-drafts/1778801234|link>.

maria: good, thanks. lisa — please add a short changelog entry and tag docs for a release note update. also open a follow-up ticket to run the failing eval set against v2.5.0 with expanded prompts (ticket: RW-13790).

kevin: if dedicated customers push back, we'll coordinate a scheduled maintenance window with account-ops. if they insist on immediate rollback we need engineering signoff because of config pin impacts. otherwise keep dedicated pinned and escalate only if customers request.

lisa: monitoring shows embed_quality back to baseline on hosted within 4m, p95 latency stable. keeping this channel updated.

maria: closing loop for now — hosted rollback complete, auto-rollback suppressed, customers notified. tagging @product for any policy follow-ups. will reconvene in 1h or sooner if dedicated customers respond. :tada:
